speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: By "standby", we are talking about both cold standby and hot standby.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Hot standby means the trains are ready to be launched if you want to.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: This is because sometimes, for example, yesterday, when you have this train with the air-con problems, you can immediately deploy a new train into the system.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What pre-emptive action, if any, is the Ministry taking to ensure that the C151C batch of trains and CT251 batches of trains that were ordered, even as the manufacturing defects were discovered which affected the C151A batch, what is the Ministry doing to ensure that this would not be repeated in future?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think when these defects occurred, would the Minister acknowledge that the main contractor, which is Kawasaki-Sifang, bears some responsibility for the quality control of the metallurgical process of the supplier because there was some impurity in the alloy, there were metallurgical issues from the supplier of the bolster.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, would not some responsibility have to be borne by the main contractor, that is, Kawasaki-Sifang, and, if so, what then is the Land Transport Authority (LTA) doing to make sure that they had done the necessary corrections to their quality control process for all suppliers?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is part of the reason why LTA originally decided to release one train at a time even though the whole process would then drag on to 2023.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think that is much more than one can hope for from any manufacturer.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Indeed, all organisations should try to emulate, including all of us in positions of responsibility, let us say, for running Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That should be the attitude we take when we confront a problem.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Take ownership, rectify it to the satisfaction of your customer.
